headframe.name: headframe
headframe.description: miningshaft covering with chests and furnaces for building.
headframe.schema_note: this is the mining cover and first chest location. its purpose is to protect entry and exit of the main mining staircase and provide chests for pickup and dropoff.
headframe.anchor_order_note: ANCHOR ORDER IS A DEADLINE, NOT A LAYOUT. Anchors 0-2 are the SHELL and must stand before nightfall: floor, walls, roof, doors, plus the chest, crafting table and furnace anchor 0 carries, because that is the minimum a fleet needs to share resources. A FURNACE AND A CHEST ARE ONE FITTING: smelting is batched for the whole fleet, so the bot that empties a furnace is usually not the bot that wanted the output, and output cannot go back into the furnace - the emptier must have somewhere to hand the surplus off. Anchor 0 is the only place in this fleet a furnace comes from; there is no pocket furnace and none is ever set down in a field. Everything that needs a surveyed MINE sits below the deadline: anchor 3 holds the rest of the stations (2 chests, 1 furnace, composter, torch). Anchors build in order and each is gated on holding ALL of its materials, so a voxel whose material comes from an unfinished chain stops the walls going up until that chain delivers. Do not move an ORE-dependent voxel into anchors 0-2.

underground_cell.name: underground_cell
underground_cell.description: 5 cubed with anchor for fractal cell mining. equal attaching on all sides. Transpose origin is in center

architect_staircase_final.name: Architect_staircase_Final
architect_staircase_final.description: 3-step diagonal descending staircase 3 wide: one walkway lane down the center, a solid wall on each side
architect_staircase_final.schema_note: GEOMETRY lives in anchors[].voxels; unassigned_voxels is empty. Voxels are transpose-origin-relative, NOT anchor-relative (collectAllVoxels pushes them raw, applying no offset) -- an anchor's position is its stand-spot, and the partition only records which stand paints each voxel; mining_executor re-assigns by reach at runtime regardless. TILING steps via attach points A(0,0,0)->B(3,-3,0) = +3,-3 per copy; repeat_offset is a DEAD FIELD read by no code -- do not trust its value. ONE LANE, THREE WIDE: the walkway is the center column z=0 and z=+-1 is solid wall wherever the walkway runs, so the body standing in the lane owns both walls and the ceiling above it. THE BOX IS FILLED SOLID ON PURPOSE (50 solid of 59 cells): a thin tube's walls are disjoint fragments -- measured 40 solid, largest face-connected group 22 -- and in rock the mountain seeds every fragment free, but in a cave nothing seeds a fragment whose every face is air. That is TessaBot's 5-loop judge-kill at 26|24|91: 3 ceiling voxels, all six neighbours air, unplaceable forever, and no ordering or retry can seed an empty set. A welded shell is ONE body, so a single attach face unzips the whole copy. Four cells stay UNDECLARED (x=2, y=-1..0, z=+-1): they are where a side-attached cell declares its door air; C and D sit in the wall plane z=+-1 directly under those doors, and mining_cell_graph:201 reads solid-vs-air as a contradiction and blackballs the cell -- the round-38 blackball, arriving from the other side. Undeclared, the cell owns them alone.

temp_construction_chest.name: temp_construction_chest
temp_construction_chest.description: when a building needs building, and the bots inventory does not have enough for the whole building then it places this blueprint reasonably close but not inside primary blueprint.

wheat_tine_row_east.name: Wheat_Tine_Row_East
wheat_tine_row_east.description: Phase-1 wheat field as TRIDENT ROWS, the east (+x) row (Architect 2026-09-15; one row split into four fixed rows 2026-09-19). FOUR ROWS INSTEAD OF ONE ROW TURNED FOUR WAYS — *"since its only 2 blocks instead of taking them and rotating them, use 2 seperate blueprints."* A bank can carry its water on any of the four sides and blueprint rotation was deleted, so the direction is now chosen by NAMING a blueprint when the row is locked, never by turning one when it is pasted. This row's land block and its two plots lie east (+x) of the stand; the other three rows are the same four blocks written the other three ways. ONE instance = ONE row of a tine built from the bank out into sea-level water: a four-block anchor — the block the bot stands on (stand_ground, external: the bank for row 0, the previous row's land block for every other row) and, in front of it, plot · land · plot. The land block is the NEXT row's stand, so the anchors overlap: stand on A(k), place A(k+1), then its two plots against it, and repeat outward. Repair runs the same way — a broken land block is rebuilt by the row behind it, which is why row 0 stands on the bank. Crop cells are the dirt voxels with a 'growing' voxel above (farmland_site); the land block is dirt with air above, so it is walked on and never tilled. The land block is listed before the plots so the place pass lays it first — a plot placed into open water has nothing else to attach to. stand_fallback false: a row whose stand does not exist yet is stranded, never tended from some other nearby block (that other block could be farmland or the wrong row). Sited only by wheat_trident_scanner (hydration, penalty-free spacing, open tip, a walking route to row 0's bank block); no water voxel, no fence.

spawn_box.name: spawn_box
spawn_box.description: the 3 cubed interior of underground_cell with the walls taken off, plus the ground it rests on — one 3x3 layer of natural floor with 3 clear layers above it, so h=4. FOUND, NEVER BUILT: the arena searches for a place that already looks like this and drops a body in it; nothing pastes it. The floor layer is 'natural_block' to say what it IS (existing terrain, not something we lay) — it is NOT checked against the natural_block item group, because that group omits every ore and a cave floor is full of them; the runtime gate is site_geometry.isGround, which is deliberately looser. The arena reads its footprint from here, the way every other siter reads a blueprint, so retune the spawn box by editing these dimensions and nothing in the bench holds a copy of the number.

spawn_spot.name: spawn_spot
spawn_spot.description: spawn_box shrunk to a SINGLE column — one natural_block floor cell with 3 clear layers above it, so h=4 like its 3x3 sibling. FOUND, NEVER BUILT. It exists to be A/B tested against spawn_box (Architect 2026-07-31: "shrink the blueprint down to a single spot… i want to see if we can increase the matches while still making good line of sight"): the 3x3 footprint is the arena predicate's scarcest clause, so shrinking it is the cheapest way to raise the match rate. What it GIVES UP is the movement room the 3x3 was demanding — a body sited here is guaranteed to FIT and is not guaranteed to be able to MOVE, which is load-bearing because BRAWLER's counter is sprint knockback. It also re-admits the 'tiny 1 by 2 cave' the 3x3 clause was written to exclude. Read arena_sites' header before making this the default.

contractor_house.name: contractor_house
contractor_house.description: this is where the standard 2 bots a contractor fleet works out of. they deposit their materials and craft here not at a players base. they dont track players chests only these.

test_house.name: test_house
test_house.description: build bench fixture. the contractor_house shell built from ONE stand, with stairs in every direction and both halves plus a chest facing away from the bot. nothing in the fleet builds it; only Auren_Workshop/tools/build_bench.js does.
test_house.schema_note: same geometry and the same single stand (0,1,0) as contractor_house. A voxel may carry a fifth element: the block state the finished cell must show, e.g. {"facing":"north","half":"top"}. The builder places such a voxel through place_authority -> facing_aim: the reported look is snapped onto the direction the rule needs for the click (stairs face the look; a chest faces opposite it) and any solid neighbour face in reach is clicked, seen or not (Architect 2026-09-16 Law 19 ruling), so no extra stand is needed for any facing. A0 floor level: bottom stairs facing east, west, north, south and a chest facing south, away from the stand. A1: wall tops carry upside-down stairs, north and south walls facing inward (the north one's full back is what the ceiling torch hangs on), west and east walls facing outward; the roof edge above them carries bottom stairs facing inward. Stair shape (corners) is decided by neighbours, not by the look, and is not asked for here.

laydown_yard.name: laydown_yard
laydown_yard.pledge_approved_note: EVERY BODY MAY PLACE AT ONCE, ONE CELL AT A TIME (Architect 2026-09-21: *'we will make blueprints explicitly labeled pledge approved. A pledge here isnt 9 blocks either its 1. If a bot can place one block then it does it. But it can claim as many as it can make. So the pledge of 1 is a minimum not a maximum... as long as the single block on the bottom is placed, the one above it can be placed.'*). The label is a CLAIM ABOUT THIS PLAN, checked at load by blueprint_registry.validatePledgeApproved: exactly one anchor, so there is no cube above a cube for a body to pillar into; and every placed voxel rests on the plan's own floor or on another placed voxel, so the per-cell support rule can always release the next block. Both are properties of the FILE, which is why they are refused on the developer's machine rather than discovered as a stalled crew.
laydown_yard.description: The builder crew's staging area for a downloaded building: 13 barrels, 14 furnaces and one crafting table, on open ground. Two parallel lines seven long, the lines 2 blocks apart: the south line is seven barrels with a furnace on each, the north line is the crafting table at its west end and six barrels, with a furnace on each of the seven (Architect 2026-10-13: the composters are gone because the crew's leaf litter and saplings go to the waste pit).
laydown_yard.schema_note: HALVED FROM 24 CONTAINERS TO 12, AND THE REASON REPLACES THE ORIGINAL ONE (Architect 2026-09-20: *"cut the blueprint in half. We shouldnt need 24 chests and furnaces because were designing with throughput in mind. That material is going to be used as gathered. So it shouldnt fill up chests."*). The 2026-09-19 design sized this yard against a QUEUE — 24 separate containers so 20 bodies would not stand in one line — and that premise no longer holds: the bot band stopped banking at all (inventory_swapper.dropOffHaul), which took barrel traffic from 33.3 openings a minute to 3.1 and the container duty cycle from 90% to 3.6% in one run. Containers are no longer the constraint, so the yard is sized for what it actually holds rather than for a queue that stopped forming. WHY BARRELS AND NOT CHESTS is unchanged: a chest will not open with a solid block on top of it and a furnace is one, while a barrel opens whatever sits above it — so barrel-under-furnace is the stacking that keeps every container usable. THE FLOOR IS NATURAL GROUND (`natural_block`): the yard sits on the ground it is sited on. EACH FURNACE SITS ON A BARREL, except the one on the crafting table; furnace_executor's fitting is a furnace with a chest registered in the fleet, which the yard's barrels are. THE COMPOSTERS BECAME BARREL-AND-FURNACE PAIRS, THE TABLE CARRIES A FURNACE AND THE CORNER OPPOSITE IT A PAIR (Architect 2026-10-13: *"compost is pointless now that we have a waste pit. exchange the 2 compost bins for another layer of furnace and barrel... put another furnace ontop of the crafting table and another barrel and furnace opposit side so each size should have 7 furances, one side has 7 barrels, the other has 6 and a crafting table"*): 13 barrels and 14 furnaces in the footprint the 12 containers had. THE AISLE IS AIR TWO HIGH so a bot walks the middle and reaches both lines from it. THE CRAFTING TABLE IS PART OF THE BUILDING NOW, not wherever the first body to need one happened to stand: craft_handler.placeStation used to site a table at nearestPlaceableCell(bot), so the fleet's shared fixtures landed together only by luck (2026-09-19). It is placed in the gap column so it obstructs neither aisle lane. EVERY BARREL AND FURNACE FACES THE AISLE (Architect 2026-10-15: *"make the furnaces face inward and the barrels laydown so its uniform. all chests and furnaces should face inward on laydown yard"*): the south line (z -2) faces south and the north line (z 1) faces north, so each fixture opens toward the bot standing in the aisle, and a barrel lies on its side like the furnace on it.
laydown_yard.anchor_order_note: ONE ANCHOR at (3,0,-1) — the floor voxel of the middle aisle — so a body STANDS at (3,1,-1), the aisle cell itself. THE +1 IS THE POINT AND IT COST A RUN: an anchor names the block a body's feet rest ON (locomotion.goToStand adds the +1, and every other blueprint in this file files its anchor on a solid voxel — planks, structural_fill, stand_ground). This anchor was authored at (3,1,-1), the aisle cell, which is authored `air` in this very voxel list — so goToStand demanded feet at (3,2,-1) with nothing under them, the navigator tried to pillar into the cell the body was already standing in, and gave up. On 2026-09-20 that was 37 of the run's 38 navigation failures and every one of the twenty bodies: the barrels were built and then unreachable, and the yard stalled at 31/53 because the builder could not reach its own stand either. Every block of the section — including the crafting table in the gap column at (0,1,-2) — is within 4.18 of the stand at (3,1,-1), inside the 4.5 reach; lowering the anchor a block IMPROVED the worst case, which was 4.77 and already over.
laydown_yard.lane_note: THE AISLE IS A ONE-WAY LANE, EAST TO WEST. A body bound for the anchor stand walks to ENTRY first (the east mouth, between the two lines' last barrels), then to the stand; a body leaving walks to EXIT first (the west mouth, in the gap column beside the crafting table), then on to wherever it is going. Both attach points follow the anchor convention: the floor block the feet rest ON. `interior` is the feet cells of the aisle between the two mouths; a route whose goal lies outside it may not enter it. `closed` is the two fixture lines, barrel level and furnace level, the whole length of each line: no route stands in a fixture's cell or on top of a barrel, built or not yet built. EXIT is the west mouth because the waste pit lies one block west of it, so a body leaving with trash is already at the rim.

waste_pit.name: waste_pit
waste_pit.description: The builder crew's waste pit: a trench two blocks long and three deep in a 4x3 pad of natural ground, where a pocket's trash is thrown to despawn (custom_api/waste_pit). The ten cells round the trench are one level floor, open two high. A thrower stands on the pad cell at either end of the trench, in line with it, and throws along it at the block under the far end's stand. Sited by the foreman beside the laydown yard.
waste_pit.anchor_order_note: TWO ANCHORS, one at each end of the trench: (1,0,0) east and (-2,0,0) west. An anchor names the block the feet rest ON, so a body stands at (1,1,0) or (-2,1,0) and reaches its own half: the hole column beside it down to its floor, and the pad cells of its two columns. The transpose origin (0,0,0) is the east hole cell, at the pad's floor level; the west hole cell is (-1,0,0).
